title: Lawyer for Masuka family says police shooting could have been averted
article: The lawyer for the family of a man shot dead New Year's eve at Toronto's St. Michael's Hospital said the tragedy could have been averted.
Lawyer Miguna Miguna said 26-year-old Henry Masuka went to the hospital as a last resort, after promised medical aid failed to arrive at his home.
Miguna said he has known Masuka and his family since they came to Canada 13 years ago.
"Emotionally they are shocked. I don't think they will come out of the shock perhaps until the test of time," he said.
Masuka took his three-month-old son Mwinula to the hospital just before midnight because he was having trouble breathing.
Toronto Police allege he took an emergency doctor hostage with a pellet gun demanding immediate medical care for his son.
The Emergency Task Force arrived and opened fire after failed negotiations with Masuka.
Masuka died of three bullet wounds to the head and chest.
Miguna said two days before the incident a doctor promised to deliver breathing equipment for Masuka's asthmatic son to his home, but it never arrived.
He also said allegations that Masuka carried an imitation pellet gun and took a doctor hostage have been fabricated.
"There is no doubt in our mind that all these allegations that are being made are completely out of character?are inconceivable," he said.
The police special investigation unit interviewed ten police officers who witnessed the incident, and have spoken to several hospital employees.
The replica pistol seized at the scene is being tested at the Centre for Forensic Sciences.
